identity.spiritualSignificanceShort: Kashi Vishwanath is revered as the shrine of Shiva as Vishvanatha, 'lord of the universe', in Varanasi, and is counted among the twelve Jyotirlingas. The lingam, about 60 cm tall and 90 cm in circumference, is housed in a silver altar. The temple stands at the centre of the Kashi pilgrimage, and since 2021 a corridor links it directly to the ghats of the Ganga.

narrative.summaryIntro:
Kashi Vishwanath Temple, located in the sacred city of Varanasi on the banks of the Ganges, is one of the most important pilgrimage sites in Hinduism. The temple is dedicated to Shiva, known here as Vishwanath (Lord of Benares), and is one of the twelve Jyotirlingas—the holiest shrines dedicated to Shiva.

The present structure was rebuilt in the 18th century by Rani Ahilya Bai Holkar of Indore. The temple's golden spire is an iconic symbol of Varanasi and stands as a testament to centuries of spiritual devotion. Millions of pilgrims visit annually seeking blessings and liberation (moksha).
narrative.documentedHistory:
The temple site in Varanasi has a long and heavily contested building history. The temple known as Adi Vishveshwar was destroyed by the Ghurids in 1194, and a mosque was raised on the site between 1236 and 1240. A rebuilt temple was demolished under Sikandar Lodi in 1490. Reconstruction began again during the reign of Akbar, initiated by Raja Man Singh and carried further by Raja Todar Mal in 1585.

In 1669 the Mughal emperor Aurangzeb destroyed the temple and the Gyanvapi Mosque was built in its place. The structure devotees visit today was built on an adjacent plot in 1780 by the Maratha ruler Ahilyabai Holkar of Indore. In 1835 the Sikh ruler Maharaja Ranjit Singh donated approximately one tonne of gold for plating the temple's dome, the origin of the gilded spire that identifies the temple.

In 1983 management of the temple passed to a board of trustees constituted by the Government of Uttar Pradesh, and the shrine is administered by the Shri Kashi Vishwanath Temple Trust. The most recent change to the site is the Shri Kashi Vishwanath Dham corridor, inaugurated on 13 December 2021, which cleared and rebuilt the congested lanes around the temple to create a roughly 1.4 km connection between the temple and the Ganga, allowing pilgrims to bathe at the river and walk directly to the shrine.

visitingInfo.nearestAirport: Lal Bahadur Shastri Airport, Varanasi, 22 km
visitingInfo.prasadInfo: The trust's paid Sugam Darshan service concludes with Mewaladdu prasad and includes a free locker and an escorted, queue-free darshan with a shastri assisting.
visitingInfo.accessibilityNotes: The trust streams a free online live darshan, which it describes as available to all devotees irrespective of physical barriers.
visitingInfo.officialContactNote: Confirm same-day darshan and aarti timings with the temple trust helpline +91 6393 131 608, or the query line 7080292930 (9:00 AM to 6:00 PM), before travelling. Timings shift on festival days. Trust office: CK 37/40,41,42 Bansphatak, Varanasi 221001.

openingHours.notes: The temple trust states the temple opens daily at 2:30 AM and closes at 11:00 PM. Darshan is not continuous through this window — aartis interrupt it; see the darshan sessions below.
The trust page states 12 Noon to 7 PM, resuming after the midday Bhog Aarti.
The trust page states evening darshan runs until 9:00 PM, after the Sapta Rishi Aarti which ends at 8:30 PM. The start time is inferred from the end of that aarti and should be confirmed.

poojas.description: The first aarti of the day, performed after the temple opens at 2:30 AM.
Midday offering of bhog; darshan is suspended during the aarti and resumes at noon.
Evening aarti; the trust lists it from 7:00 PM to 8:30 PM.
The closing aarti; the temple closes at 11:00 PM.

festivals.significance: Night of Shiva; thousands of devotees perform all-night vigils and prayers
Full moon; special rituals and massive congregation
